description: v1.17 (review X-2): ASSUMED order-entry latency per source venue, written into an ingested real dataset's configs/venues/venues.json by iap.marketdata.ingest (real feeds carry exchange timestamps only, so nothing here is measured). mean_ns is the MEAN of the simulator's base + U[0, jitter_ns] draw (iap.execution.realism.simulator_latency_base_ns converts). The values equal configs/prereg/v3.json venue_latency; a pre-registration's venue_latency overrides them. v2.0 stage 2 D4 (D-06): feed_delay is the DECLARED market-data delay the execution replay applies when a caller does not pass md_delay_ns (iap.execution.latency.declared_feed_delay): the replayed event stamped exchange_ts at t is seen at t + default_ns. It is an assumption (real ITCH and IEX HIST carry exchange time only; the IEX capture offset is unknown), never a measurement, and never zero by default. engine_decision_to_arrival_ns is the engine's one fill-price convention (E0 section 9 / C8; iap.execution.sim.LATENCY_NS asserts equality); sensitivity_steps_ns is the plan 5.9 grid every execution number is reported at.

feed_delay.label: assumed
feed_delay.provenance: configs/prereg/v2.json and v3.json feed_latency_ns (100 us, the primary assumed feed leg of the maker and quoting backtests since v1.14); chosen as the one declared value so every route states the same assumption unless it declares its own

default.receive_ts: receive_ts == exchange_ts in the data (the feed carries exchange time only); the replay sees the event at exchange_ts + md_delay_ns

itch50.receive_ts: receive_ts == exchange_ts (Nasdaq TotalView-ITCH 5.0 sample files carry the exchange timestamp only; no capture stamp exists); seen at exchange_ts + md_delay_ns

iex-deep-plus.receive_ts: receive_ts == exchange_ts (IEX HIST messages carry IEX's UTC send timestamp; the pcap capture stamp is NOT used on this route); seen at exchange_ts + md_delay_ns

iex-deep.receive_ts: receive_ts == exchange_ts (as iex-deep-plus; price levels, synthetic orders); seen at exchange_ts + md_delay_ns

iex-capture.receive_ts: receive_ts = the capture host's packet stamp (ingest --capture-ts, datasets iex_capts/*): receive_ts - exchange_ts contains an unidentified constant offset (about 37 s, TAI-stamped host), so only within-capture differences are interpretable and no absolute feed latency is claimed; the replay still applies md_delay_ns to exchange_ts, it does not read the capture stamp

synthetic.receive_ts: receive_ts = exchange_ts + the generator's drawn latency (iap.marketdata generate); the replay applies md_delay_ns on top, as for a real route
